docs.purpose: Forces an immediate recomputation of today's data-quality snapshot — permit counts, trade-match rates, builder enrichment, property linkage and so on — instead of waiting for the next scheduled capture, so the quality dashboard reflects current numbers on demand.
docs.data_story: It reads 9 tables — `permits`, `permit_trades`, `entities`, `permit_parcels`, `coa_applications`, `building_footprints`, `parcel_buildings`, `permit_inspections` and `sync_runs` and writes `data_quality_snapshots`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: No SPEC LINK header. A 20-line handler whose entire body delegates to captureDataQualitySnapshot() in src/lib/quality/metrics.ts, which fans out roughly sixteen parallel counting queries across the listed tables and upserts one row per day into data_quality_snapshots (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE). No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: THE CLASSIFICATION QUESTION (both line numbers): '/api/quality/refresh' appears in AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122 and '/api/quality' appears in PUBLIC_PREFIXES at src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:75. classifyRoute tests AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES FIRST at route-guard.ts:165 and returns at :166; the PUBLIC_PREFIXES test is at :170. Because :166 returns, :170 is unreachable for this path — AUTHENTICATED WINS. So this route is NOT public, despite the task brief's premise. Consequence a reviewer must know: the handler carries NO in-handler auth (route.ts:9 takes no request and calls no guard), so authentication rests ENTIRELY on middleware ordering. If someone ever reorders those two branches, or adds a sibling like /api/quality/refresh-all (which would match only the public prefix), this write endpoint silently becomes anonymous. It is also UNAUTHENTICATED-EQUIVALENT in dev: src/middleware.ts:49-77 short-circuits every non-public route when isDevMode() (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:33). Second finding: it is an unrestricted work trigger — any authenticated user (no admin check, no rate limit) can fire 16 parallel full-table aggregate queries (src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:25-42, Promise.all over COUNT(*)-class scans of permits/permit_trades/entities/coa_applications/permit_parcels/permit_inspections) and overwrite today's data_quality_snapshots row. The write is idempotent per day (ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE, metrics.ts:167) so it is not destructive across days, but it does let a non-admin rewrite the row /api/quality then serves publicly. Two branches match this exact path and the ORDER decides it. (1) AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES contains the exact string '/api/quality/refresh' (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:122) and is tested at route-guard.ts:165 — `pathname === r` is true, so classifyRoute RETURNS 'authenticated' at route-guard.ts:166. (2) PUBLIC_PREFIXES contains '/api/quality' (route-guard.ts:75) and is tested at route-guard.ts:170 — `startsWith` would also be true, but line 170 is NEVER REACHED for this path because line 166 already returned.
